answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Proof of unique operating system install date changes that arithmetic: an OS installed two years ago, so the copper for each fake is paid in the real world. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own an OS installed two years ago, and the pigment grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the delta of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
